passages.note: Assembly concurrence vote on the chaptered SAFETY Act text; Blanca Rubio is listed among the Ayes and 16 of 77 voting were No, so not near-unanimous.

passages.provision_quote: shall not enact or enforce any policy, rule, or administrative regulation that would require an employee or a contractor to disclose any information related to a pupil’s sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression to any other person without the pupil’s consent, unless otherwise required by state or federal law.
passages.note: Chaptered text she voted for on concurrence; the operative section forbids rules requiring disclosure without consent but does not require staff to withhold it (the 'Coauthor: Senator Rubio' line is a different legislator).

rows.reasoning: Blanca Rubio voted Aye (61-16) on concurrence in AB 1955 (2023-2024), whose operative Section 220.5 says a school district "shall not enact or enforce any policy, rule, or administrative regulation that would require an employee or a contractor to disclose" a pupil's gender identity without consent, matching the rung "Forbid rules that require schools to tell parents." The bill only bars compelled disclosure and does not require staff to keep the information from parents, so it does not reach "Require staff to keep a student's gender identity from parents unless the student consents", and it excludes the notification rungs.
